Mechanism family: pareto-knapsack-frontier-decomposition
Replacement scope: Add a new construction phase before the SA loop in `compute_model_placement`; its output seeds the SA (which replaces the current seed list).
Compute budget: DP over scaled integer sizes with a cap of ~2000 memory units per GPU and dominance-pruned load states (≤ ~2000·n states per pass, one pass); negligible added time (<0.1s expected).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent searches the assignment space point-by-point and never reasons about what (memory, load) combinations a single GPU can realize. A per-GPU Pareto frontier enumerates all non-dominated (used_memory, total_load) pairs achievable by any subset of models (classic subset-sum DP with load accumulation and dominance pruning: state (m, L) dominates (m', L') if m ≤ m' and L ≤ L'). Then a global selection step picks one frontier point per GPU (with points partitioning the model set via backpointers, or via a greedy realization pass) minimizing max over GPUs of L/(MEM−m). This directly optimizes the true ratio objective on a compressed representation, escaping the incumbent's greedy basin entirely. Feasibility: DP only enumerates subsets with used memory ≤ GPU_MEM_SIZE, so any realized point is feasible; if the DP cannot cover all models, fall back to incumbent seeds.
